messages:
Jordan (support): Heads up — BrightDoc reporting spikes of 504s and 5xx from hosted API, started ~11:04 PT. Customer traces show long queuing + 'request_queue_overflow'. They're high on small, bursty requests.
Maria (eng-sre): Got it. Can you paste a sample X-Request-ID and a curl we can replay? Any specific endpoint or payload pattern?
Jordan (support): Sample curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Request-ID: rq-abc123\" -d '{"text":"short prompt"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
Jordan (support): Request IDs: rq-abc123, rq-abc124, rq-abc125. Pattern: many concurrent short requests (50–100 qps) in bursts, ~20–30ms client RTT. Customer says errors are intermittent but spike with bursts.
Kevin (oncall): Looking at infra metrics now — gateway p95 queue time jumped to 2.1s, host queue_depth at ~240/256 on several nodes. Continuous-batcher backlog is growing; dequeue rate dropped. Quick log snippet from gateway: ```[2026-03-17T18:04:12Z] warn gateway queue_depth=240/256 tenant=brightdoc tail_timeout=1.23s dequeued=0 enqueue=120```
Sasha (eng-runtime): Pulling runtime logs, I see repeated batcher warnings: ```WARN batcher: backlog_size=184 -> cannot form batch within max_wait_ms; KV-cache-evict lock contention; defer_eviction failure``` Dequeue loop is hitting timeouts: `dequeue timed out after 500ms` a few hundred times over the last minute.
Maria (eng-sre): Likely combo: very bursty short reqs + KV cache eviction lockups causing batcher to stall and queue to saturate. Short-term mitigation options: 1) reduce batch wait from 40ms -> 10ms for affected pool, 2) apply per-tenant ingress rate cap, 3) temporarily bump max_queue_depth or add more replicas. Which should we try first?
Kevin (oncall): I triggered scale-up on the hosted pool (added 2 replicas) and applied a tenant soft-limit of 60rps for BrightDoc. Also pushed a config to reduce batch wait to 10ms for the pool leader for quick rollout. Monitoring now.
deploy-bot: automated: `scale up hosted/pool-3 +2 replicas` succeeded. config apply: `batch.window_ms=10` rolled to 2/3 hosts.
support-bot: Message sent to customer: "We applied mitigations (temporary rate cap + pool scale-up + reduced batch wait). Can you confirm if errors drop and share any other traffic patterns?" :mailbox_with_mail:
Jordan (support): Customer reports error rate dropped from ~12% -> ~1% within 90s after the changes. They still see occasional tail timeouts on long seq requests (seq > 1024).
Sasha (eng-runtime): Good. For follow-up: runtime will add extra telemetry around batcher dequeue latencies and KV eviction timeouts. I already captured heap of traces for the failing dequeues for postmortem.
Maria (eng-sre): Root cause hypothesis: continuous-batcher backlog created by bursty short requests combined with KV eviction stalls -> queue saturation -> tail timeouts. Action items: create infra JIRA (INF-7421) to investigate KV eviction lock behavior and introduce stronger tenant backpressure in gateway. Also add a runbook step to prefer scale-up + priority routing before bumping max_queue_depth.
Kevin (oncall): Created JIRA INF-7421, assigned eng-runtime + infra. I'll follow up with the customer later today and leave this thread open until we confirm stability for 24h.
Jordan (support): Noted — customer confirmed they see much improved success rate and appreciate the quick mitigation. Keeping monitoring on.
Maria (eng-sre): Postmortem notes: include timeline, mitigations, metric graphs (queue depth, batcher backlog, dequeue latency), and recommended long-term fixes (per-tenant adaptive rate limiting, KV eviction retry improvements, smarter batching heuristics). Putting runbook link in JIRA.
deploy-bot: runbook: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/queue-saturation-mitigation
Kevin (oncall): Closing initial escalation for now, will reopen if error rate > 5% for 5m. :thumbsup:
